insight: The syntax highlighting in Markdown.tsx's renderHighlightedTree() uses nested <Text> elements with different color props per token. Ink's Yoga layout miscalculates inline flow for nested <Text> with different colors, inserting spurious line breaks between tokens. This is the same class of bug that MultilineTextInput's renderWithCursor() works around by using raw ANSI escape codes instead of nested <Text inverse>. The fix should follow the same pattern: render each line as a single <Text> with ANSI color codes embedded in the string.

LSP ergonomics implementation: The key architectural insight was that parsePositionInput needed to become async to support text/symbol resolution (which requires reading files from disk and making LSP requests). This rippled through all 14 cursor-position tools. The NormalizedSymbol type has optional line/column fields, so resolveSymbolPosition needed type-narrowing filters to handle symbols without position info. The test pattern of creating a minimal ServerManager with no real LSP servers worked well for testing text resolution in isolation.

The file__apply_diff tool consistently fails on files with certain content patterns (e.g., when context lines contain only whitespace or the @@ heading doesn't match exactly). For multi-line code insertions in TypeScript files, using a Python script with string replacement and assertions is more reliable than the diff tool. This was observed during the MCP roots capability implementation where all 13+ edits to client.ts were applied via Python instead of file__apply_diff.

Planned syntax highlighting fixes: (1) background width padding in renderHighlightedTree(), (2) configurable syntax colors via new DroneTuiConfig type in drone-core. Config threads through App → ChatLog/AssistantMessageBlock → Markdown. Plan saved as project memory 'tui-issue2-syntax-highlighting-fix'.

When threading new props through App.tsx's conversation event listener, use refs (like syntaxColorsRef) to avoid stale closure issues. The event listener is a useEffect that captures variables at setup time; refs let it read the latest values without re-registering the listener on every change.

The `file__apply_diff` tool's `renderComponent` registration was tricky because all 5 file tool registrations have identical context lines (`additionalProperties: false,\n      },\n      execute: async input => {`), causing `file__apply_diff` patches to land in the wrong spot. Had to rewrite the entire file to fix it. Lesson: when patching files with identical context blocks, use more unique context or write the whole file.

The subagent dispatch tool now has real-time NDJSON event streaming from the subagent's stdout. Each NDJSON event (reasoning, toolCall, assistantMessage, return) is parsed as it arrives and emitted via onProgress() with a prefixed string format (reasoning:, tool:, msg:, done:). This pattern is reusable for any future feature that needs to monitor subagent progress in real time — the infrastructure (onProgress callback, outputLines accumulation in app.tsx, custom renderComponent) is already in place.

Meta-tool pretty output plan: The list_tools/mount_tool/unmount_tool meta-tools across git, swarm, and MCP plugins are structurally identical but return slightly different JSON shapes (MCP includes serverId, uses different field names). A single set of 3 reusable components (ListToolsBlock, MountToolBlock, UnmountToolBlock) can serve all three plugins if we normalize the MCP result shapes. The plan is saved as project memory 'meta-tool-pretty-output'.

The file__apply_diff tool struggles with multi-hunk patches on files that have already been partially patched. When applying multiple changes to the same file, it's more reliable to write the complete file with file__write than to apply sequential patches. The patch tool also has issues with indentation-sensitive patches where the context lines have different indentation than expected — it can insert lines at wrong positions or create duplicate properties.

OpenAI and OpenRouter use different JSON formats for reasoning effort in their API requests. OpenAI uses a top-level `reasoning_effort` (snake_case string), while OpenRouter uses a nested `reasoning: { effort: string }` object. The solution was to add both fields to the shared `OpenAiChatRequest` type and let each plugin set the field its API expects. The API ignores fields it doesn't understand, so this is safe and avoids conditional logic.

OpenRouter returns `reasoning` inside `choice.message.reasoning` (as a field on the message object), not at `choice.reasoning` like OpenAI does. The shared `fromOpenAiResponse` adapter only checked `choice.reasoning`, so OpenRouter reasoning was silently dropped. Fixed by adding `reasoning?: string` to `OpenAiMessage` type and adding a fallback check in `fromOpenAiResponse` that checks `choice.message.reasoning` when `choice.reasoning` is absent. Choice-level still takes precedence when both are present.

When using file__apply_diff on multiple files in a session, some patches may silently fail to apply (e.g., when the file content has changed since the patch was generated). Always verify patches were applied by checking git diff or running typecheck after each batch of changes. In this session, several core type patches were lost and had to be re-applied manually.

Coordinator UI has a dual-session-table problem: `beacon_sessions` tracks per-beacon agent connections (with disconnected_at), while `swarm_sessions` tracks the overall session lifecycle (with status field). The terminate flow only touched beacon_sessions, leaving swarm_sessions stuck on 'active'. The fix adds a POST /sessions/:id/end endpoint that updates swarm_sessions, and the UI calls it after the beacon DELETE regardless of whether the beacon session was already ended.

The coordinator has two separate session tables (beacon_sessions and swarm_sessions) that can get out of sync. The terminate flow only updated beacon_sessions, leaving swarm_sessions stuck on 'active'. The fix adds a POST /sessions/:id/end endpoint that directly updates swarm_sessions, and the UI calls it after the beacon DELETE regardless of whether the beacon session was already ended. This pattern should be kept in mind for future session lifecycle work.

The /api prefix migration touched more files than initially scoped. The drone-gateway package also has a CoordinatorClient class that calls coordinator API routes directly, and its tests needed updating too. When doing cross-package API path changes, always search for all consumers of the API across the entire monorepo, not just the obvious ones (coordinator + UI + beacon).

Coordinator UI active persona bug fix: The root cause was that the swarm plugin registers the agent session with the beacon at `onPluginsLoaded` (with `personaId: null`), but the persona plugin activates the persona at `onSessionStart` (which fires later). The fix adds a complete pipeline: (1) a PATCH endpoint on the coordinator for updating session persona, (2) a PATCH endpoint on the beacon for updating agent persona, (3) a coordinator client method on the beacon, (4) a hook function in the swarm plugin, and (5) a subscription to persona changes in the swarm plugin's index. Also added `activePersona` to event metadata for audit trail.

The mid-panel widget system in tui/app.tsx uses a hardcoded list of known plugin IDs and a useRef that doesn't trigger re-renders. This should be rearchitected to support dynamic registration from any plugin (including external/user plugins) with custom React components. Punted to roadmap — needs its own planning session.

When removing a dependency from a plugin's deps type (like budgetService from CompactionPluginDeps), the test file must also be updated. The initial code-quality-cleanup commit missed updating compaction.test.ts, which caused 15 LSP errors. Always grep for the removed field name in test files as part of the validation step.

The plan persona sometimes slips into implementation mode for trivial fixes. The project workflow accepts this — it's not worth fighting. The important thing is the fix is correct, not which persona wrote it. This is a pragmatic design choice: the workflow is resilient to role bleed.

The commits spanned 5 major features: Web UI Management Console (5.5), MitM verification, approval token improvements, live event streaming + /api prefix, active persona propagation, and code quality cleanup. The `file__apply_diff` tool struggles with files that have duplicate property names in object literals (TypeScript error 1117). When a patch creates duplicates, the tool's fuzz matching can apply hunks to the wrong location, compounding the problem. The safest approach when dealing with duplicate properties is to write the entire file content via `file__write` rather than trying to surgically remove duplicates with `file__apply_diff`.

Converted LSP and file plugins to list-mount pattern. Key learnings: (1) The file plugin's tools were defined inline (not in separate factory files), so the conversion required extracting each tool object literal and passing it to `fileCache.addTool()` instead of `registration.registerTool()`. (2) The LSP plugin's tools were already in factory functions, making the conversion straightforward — just swap the registration loop for cache additions. (3) Both plugins now follow the exact same pattern as the git plugin: 3 meta-tools + ToolMountingCache + optional persona dependency. (4) The file test file needed `mountTool()` calls before each tool usage, which was a mechanical but thorough change across ~46 tests.

The useBracketedPaste hook's debounce fallback has a subtle behavior: the first character is always delivered immediately because lastCharTimeRef starts at 0 (Date.now() - 0 > 30ms). This means rapid pastes without bracketed paste support will have the first character delivered immediately and the rest buffered and flushed as a single string after 50ms. This is acceptable behavior — the user sees the first character appear instantly, then the rest appears atomically after a brief pause. For bracketed paste (the primary mechanism), the entire paste is delivered atomically with no perceptible delay.

TUI paste rendering bug: Ink's output engine (output.js) splits text on 
 only. A  character survives as a literal character in the rendered output, causing the terminal to perform a carriage return (cursor jumps to column 0 on the same line) instead of advancing to the next line. This was the root cause of pasted newlines not rendering correctly — the clipboard/terminal was sending 
 or bare , and the useBracketedPaste hook was delivering them as-is. Fix: normalize 
 → 
 and  → 
 in useBracketedPaste.ts at all four delivery points (bracketed paste split-chunk, bracketed paste single-chunk, debounce flush, debounce immediate). The order matters: replace 
 first, then remaining , to avoid double-converting 
 to 

.

The /systemprompt slash command manually assembles its output from config.systemPrompt + renderPromptFragments(), bypassing buildSystemMessages() from the context budget service. This means the runtime flags block (list-mount explainer, active plugins) is sent to the LLM but invisible to the user. The fix is to add buildSystemMessages to the engine interface, wire it from the budget service in index.tsx, and have the /systemprompt handler use it. This is tracked in plan-fix-systemprompt-runtime-flags.

When adding a new method to the DronePluginEngine interface, you must also add it to the DroneTuiOptions.engine Pick type in tui/types.ts, otherwise the TUI won't compile. This is a common gotcha when extending the engine surface.

When planning multi-language LSP support, we identified two tiers of project language detection: (1) heuristic detection for well-known languages with known LSP servers (reuse bootstrap's project detection), and (2) LLM-assisted detection for everything else (deferred to 5.10.2). The LLM-assisted approach was deemed a good candidate for a user-customizable macro rather than a complex built-in system. This two-tier pattern could apply to other "detect and configure" features.

When extending the DronePluginEngine interface with new methods, you must also add them to the DroneTuiOptions.engine Pick type in tui/types.ts, otherwise the TUI won't compile. This is a recurring gotcha — it happened again with buildSystemMessages and now with getAvailableServers/startServerForFile (though the LSP plugin doesn't use TUI types directly, the pattern is the same for any engine method exposed to TUI).

The Go module proxy (proxy.golang.org) supports both .zip and .tar.gz formats for module downloads. Using .tar.gz is simpler because the existing tar extraction infrastructure handles it directly — no need for a zip library dependency. The URL pattern is: https://proxy.golang.org/{module}/@v/{version}.tar.gz

LSP Hash Fix planning revealed several hidden issues beyond just computing hashes: (1) gopls URL returns 404 for .tar.gz, needs .zip + build step, (2) DroneLspInstallSpec lacks platform-awareness for platform-specific binary tarballs, (3) rust-analyzer and lua-language-server need ARM variants. The plan covers all of these in a single pass.
